**GM, Readers!**

The Fed decides today. The Senate voted yesterday. And whales have been quietly repositioning for weeks. Strategy bought back $139M of $STRC preferred stock. Bitmine surpasses the 5.96M ETH threshold. Lazarus sold 911 ETH over a two-hour window.

# 🐋 THE BIG WHALE MOVES

### **1. Strategy's $139M Preferred Buyback (No BTC Movement)**

Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy)[ repurchased](https://assets.contentstack.io/v3/assets/bltf8d808d9b8cebd37/bltfd690f9e2425297b/6aa74f1cd8141fe81e6db03b/form-8-k_09-14-2026.pdf) $139M of its $STRC preferred shares between Sept 8-13, funded entirely from USD cash. Bitcoin holdings remained unchanged at **845,050 BTC**. The company now sits on $6.4B in USD assets alongside its massive BTC stack.

This is the second consecutive week with zero Bitcoin purchases or sales. Strategy has shifted capital allocation toward retiring preferred equity while keeping the core BTC treasury intact.

**Whale Intel: **When the largest corporate Bitcoin holder chooses buybacks over accumulation for multiple weeks, it is a signal of balance-sheet priority, not a change in the long-term thesis.

BitMine Immersion Technologies (BMNR)[ announced](https://www.prnewswire.com/in/news-releases/bitmine-immersion-technologies-bmnr-announces-eth-holdings-reach-5-96-million-tokens-and-total-crypto-and-total-cash-holdings-of-15-8-billion-302877165.html) Monday that it bought another 27,180 ETH last week, taking total holdings to 5,956,378 ETH. Combined crypto plus cash plus moonshot investments now stand at $15.8B, per the company's press release.

Welcome back! A model with no output to speak of, Salesforce moving into Claude, Siri finally arriving after years of delays, and 30 Chinese researchers treating recursive self-improvement as a finish line.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: A new kind of AI model launched by ChatGPT co-creator: What does a model cost when the output tokens are free? Salesforce now lives inside Claude: How many sales tasks work out of the box, and what can Claude see? Siri AI is finally out: Which number makes this the biggest AI rollout so far? The Last AI Built by Humans: What sits at Level 5, and why is Western AI treating it as a risk? PS: Want to collaborate with the biggest GTM engine and distribution moat for AI companies? You can feature your tool with us and reach millions. A new kind of AI model launched by ChatGPT co-creator Diogo Almeida, formerly of OpenAI, brought TypeSafe out of stealth with Jev.  It answers preset questions inside software and attaches a confidence score to each answer. The numbers:  → $42 per billion input tokens, with output free → TypeSafe puts that at 238x cheaper than Claude Fable 5.1 → Responses in 70 to 500 milliseconds, which is 40 to 200x faster than current LLMs The pitch is that Jev cannot hallucinate, because it picks between options defined in advance.  Almeida calls it a frontier-intelligence function call and says it behaves more like a database than a coworker. Worth being precise about that claim.  A constrained output space means it cannot invent a fact, and it can still choose the wrong option from the list.  The confidence score is doing real work there, since it tells you when the pick is shaky. What it's for: fast judgment calls inside applications.  Routing a request to the right queue, scoring a record, screening another model's output for jailbreak attempts. The name is a nod to Jevons paradox, which says that as something gets cheaper people use far more of it.  If the speed and price hold up in production, this stops being a product you evaluate and becomes a component you drop into everything. Claude, from first prompt to production Most people learn Claude by accident. A prompt here, a workaround there, and six months later they're still using it like a search box. Today in AI NOW & BEYOND 🔥 RAG That Actually Understands Tables, Charts, and Diagrams Mother Says Meta AI Dug Into Her Children’s Details and Location AI Highlights of the Week Too Important to Miss RAG That Actually Understands Tables, Charts, and Diagrams Most RAG pipelines struggle when documents contain more than plain text. Tables lose their structure, charts get skipped, and diagrams don't translate well into embeddings. VultronRetriever brings multimodal retrieval to RAG with open-weight models that treat PDF pages as images, preserving visual context while using late-interaction retrieval to find the most relevant pages. With strong ViDoRe V3 results, you can self-host the models or run them through Vultr Serverless Inference. See VultronRetriever in Action! Mother Says Meta AI Dug Into Her Children’s Details and Location The company says it fixed intrusive prompts after a family video triggered unexpected questions Kalie Robins shared a video of herself singing with her daughter. She says Meta AI then suggested questions that pulled together personal information from years of family posts. Key Points: Her Children’s Details: The chatbot gathered names, birth information and photos of both daughters, including material posted by relatives. A Search for Home: Robins says it suggested asking where she lived, then connected older and newer posts to pinpoint her location. A Photo She Thought Was Gone: Robins says the chatbot also resurfaced a picture she had deleted years earlier. Meta Acknowledges the Problem: Meta says it fixed the inappropriate suggestions, while stressing that answers only draw on information the user can already access. Why It Matters: The privacy concern is not just what people share, but what AI can piece together from it. A birthday post, an old photo, and a family video can reveal far more together than their owners intended.
